question: why cant we determine the position of an electron in an atom

info.headline: Why can't we determine the position of an electron in an atom

annotations.label: Electrons
annotations.text: We cannot precisely determine the exact position of an electron because the act of measuring its position alters its momentum, and electrons fundamentally exist as diffuse probability clouds rather than particles following fixed trajectories.

changes.label: Electrons
changes.text: As an electron's speed increases, determining its position can theoretically be done with greater precision because higher momentum allows for finer resolution during measurement, though its momentum simultaneously becomes much more uncertain.
